reasoning: Identity confirmed: number 7565, February 27, 1937, Franklin D. Roosevelt, title match the held GPO printing, the HathiTrust GPO printing and the census register; the WPA list agrees on the until-date. The order has one operative sentence (exempt Austin from section 204 and continue him in service until March 1, 1938); the single clause covering characters 213-1401 is a complete inventory. The end by own terms on 1938-03-01, actor the order, mechanism expiration by own terms, is recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading stated as the until-dates ruling requires. No earlier end appears: no held text cites EO 7565 by number, the name search finds only EO 6976 (the earlier exemption this order recites) and EO 7565, and the only OFR note for the order is 'Amends: EO 6976', which the claim's account of the recital addresses. No separation, death or retirement before the date appears in held sources. No savings or independent command exists. The working-text grade and standing note are labeled correctly. Notes (not defects): a held HathiTrust GPO printing graded official_printing (photius-gpo-volumes) gives the same wording and could serve as a better-custody working text; the namier person-name search reports 0 hits for this order although EO 6976 names Austin (it appears to count only other later texts), which the claim discloses by reporting its own separate name search.

reasoning: Identity, text and inventory are sound: EO 11963 of January 19, 1977 (42 FR 4325) has two sections, both amending EO 10900, and both are inventoried. The legal analysis in the reasons is supportable: under the strike-and-insert ruling both amendments run with EO 10900, which EO 12220 section 1-501 revoked as amended; EO 12148 and EO 12163 touch other sections, so no earlier end appears; the OFR 'Revoked by: EO 12220, June 27, 1980' note is consistent with that analysis. But every structured end date (both clause first_end dates and whole_order_end) reads 1977-06-27, a date that matches no source: EO 12220 is dated June 27, 1980, its cited source carries signing_date 1980-06-27, and the claim's own reasons say June 27, 1980. A 1977-06-27 end would also falsely place the revocation three years before the revoking order existed. The claim is rejected for the wrong date and the internal inconsistency. Secondary defect: the savings reason calls the EO 12220 consultation 'the same' when its list of officials differs. Note (not a defect): the clause sources from fr-originals carry no grade field; the claim also does not cite the OFR 'Revoked by' note by name, though it addresses the same instrument.
